solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food, something in freezer on right

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

parts.note: ice is what a freezer makes

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out where the food sits in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICE is written after the R, which is what 'on' asks for in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the grain is one of the world's staple foods, so 'Food' names the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Boost has excited archer, eg

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An archer, say, gets a lift from excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg' looks like it introduces an example, but its two letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by metaphor: topping up a flat battery is the image behind giving someone's energy a boost.

clue.text: Tea bags in tea cups etc

parts.note: used as it stands, placed inside CH…A

explanation.surface: Tea bags sitting in the cups ready for brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' reads as the thing you dunk; here 'bags' is a verb and 'Tea' is CHA holding IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective noun: the word covers cups, saucers and plates made of porcelain, and 'etc' admits the rest of the set.

clue.text: Piano, scratched on the outside, thrown on rubbish tip

explanation.surface: A battered piano, scratched all over, is dumped at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the thing being dumped, but it is just the musical abbreviation; the extra P is why the answer has a double letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something junked as worthless ends up at the tip, and the adjective matches the past participle 'thrown'.

clue.text: New topic on mental thought

indicators.note: a new form of the letters: they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh subject about mental thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as a preposition but its letters belong in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun 'thought' in its sense of quiet reflection, as in 'lost in thought'.

clue.text: Overturned sheet on which is a pseudonym

indicators.note: turned upside down: in a down answer, read bottom to top
in a down answer, what sits on top comes first

parts.note: a sheet is a sail, and sail turned over is LIAS

explanation.surface: A capsized boat's sail, with someone's false name painted on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' suggests bedding or paper; on a boat a sheet is also a sail, the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name an assumed name used in place of your real one.

clue.text: Paul ate off table

indicators.note: gone bad, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Paul, eating straight off the table without a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' reads as furniture, but it is tableland: a flat-topped high plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical sense: 'table' or tableland is raised ground with a flat top, like Table Mountain.

clue.text: Go out as part of crowd at event

indicators.note: the answer forms only a part of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of 'crowd', through 'at', into the start of 'event'

explanation.surface: Slipping out of a party while mingling with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: crowD AT Event: the answer bridges three words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go out with someone is to be romantically seeing them, so the verbs match.

clue.text: The law reforms in plentiful supply

indicators.note: forms again: the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Legal reforms arriving in abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun in a news headline; here it is a verb telling THE LAW to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary sense: beyond riches, the word means an abundance, as in 'a wealth of detail'.

clue.text: Greek character accompanied by slim South American

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person travelling with a thin South American companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece; in crosswords it is usually a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a person from Chile is one kind of South American.

clue.text: Coloured paint unsuitable

indicators.note: coloured means distorted or altered, so the letters change

explanation.surface: A decorator rejecting a coloured paint as the wrong shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coloured' fits paint so naturally that it hides its job: as in 'coloured by prejudice', it means distorted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the negative prefix on 'apt' (fitting) gives an adjective meaning not fitting.

clue.text: Ever a grown-up?

parts.note: a grown-up child has grown tall

explanation.surface: A wistful question: was I ever really an adult?
explanation.walkthrough: 'grown-up' reads as a noun, an adult; it is taken as an adjective, grown up tall.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: in questions and negatives the two are interchangeable, as in 'did you ever doubt it?'

clue.text: Consumer embraces beginning of song festival

explanation.surface: A shopper swept up in a song festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer' suggests a shopper; here it is someone who consumes food.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the spring Christian feast of the resurrection is one festival among many.

clue.text: Loose as it were, most ready to drop

indicators.note: the letters are set loose and re-form

explanation.surface: Something hanging loose, on the point of falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready to drop' pairs with 'Loose' to suggest a falling object; it means exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'ready to drop' is dead tired, and the superlative matches 'most'.

clue.text: Succeed as paparazzo — see?

definitions.meaning: a paparazzo succeeds by landing the photo

explanation.surface: A celebrity photographer landing the shot, and asking if you follow.
explanation.walkthrough: A paparazzo is a photographer who chases celebrities. 'see?' is the everyday 'understand?', not looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally, a photographer securing the shot; as an idiom, grasping the situation, which is what 'see?' asks.

clue.text: Bit of a daffy instrument!

definitions.meaning: the frilled central tube of a daffodil, short here to 'daffy'

explanation.surface: A slightly silly musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daffy' means silly, but here it is short for daffodil, whose frilled centre is named after the brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the brass instrument, and the flared corona of a daffodil, which is shaped like its bell.

clue.text: Critical moment, sound of teeth on Corn Flakes?

definitions.meaning: the decisive point when a matter comes to a head

definitions.text: sound of teeth on Corn Flakes
definitions.meaning: the noise of biting dry cereal

explanation.surface: A tense moment at breakfast, spoon poised over the cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half needs no trick: it simply describes the noise, and the phrase 'when it comes to the crunch' gives the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an idiom for the decisive moment, and the imitative word for biting something brittle.

clue.text: Two articles written by chap in country

parts.note: the indefinite articles AN and A

explanation.surface: A man who wrote a pair of newspaper pieces while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means the grammatical articles A and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the former British colony on South America's north coast is one country among many.

clue.text: Letter a prickly thing?

parts.note: an itch is a prickling feeling

explanation.surface: A letter described as a prickly thing, like a thorny note.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is how the letter H is spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the spelt-out name of H, one letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Blade losing its edge, say

indicators.note: a word's edge is its outermost letter, here the front one

explanation.surface: A knife that has gone blunt, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing its edge' fits a blade going blunt; here the edge is the first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to speak words aloud, as in 'she didn't say a word'.

clue.text: Performer in gutter, one tanked up

indicators.note: the letters are inside the following words
in a down answer, going up means reading backwards

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of 'gutter', all of 'one' and the start of 'tanked'; 'up' then reverses them

explanation.surface: A drunken busker lying in the gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanked up' reads as drunk, but 'up' is detached to reverse the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a singer in the high male voice range is one kind of performer.

clue.text: Head scratched in difficult argument

indicators.note: to scratch is to strike out, and the head is the first letter

parts.note: stiff = difficult, as a stiff test

explanation.surface: Someone scratching their head during a tricky argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head scratched' is a puzzled gesture; here it means the front letter is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, narrowed: a petty quarrel between people close to each other is a small argument.

clue.text: Popular place for contribution

explanation.surface: A popular venue asking for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' reads as a noun, a venue; it is the verb, to put.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what someone adds to a discussion or project, as in 'thanks for your contribution'.

clue.text: Perfume in smell, might you say?

indicators.note: points to how the phrase would be spoken

parts.note: a smell is a scent, so 'in smell' becomes 'in scents'

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a perfume is really just a nice smell.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks you to translate 'smell' before speaking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means both fragrant smoke and, more loosely, any sweet perfume.

clue.text: Lovely dog's activity?

definitions.meaning: dogs bring back thrown sticks and balls

explanation.surface: A lovely dog at play.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as an example: bringing back a ball is one thing dogs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for attractive, and the present participle of the verb for retrieving a thrown stick.

clue.text: Brood in ferment at regular intervals

indicators.note: letters taken at evenly spaced gaps: here every second one, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Stewing over something while agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferment' tempts as a synonym for brood; it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to dwell anxiously on a worry.
